_about: Example ceremony manifest for the README walkthrough: sudo ./install.sh --mode api --manifest ceremony.json
JSON has no comments, so every key starting with '_' is documentation; install.sh and cutover.sh ignore them.
Public values are filled in (XPR testnet chain id, the Tahoe network, the pulse-cutover release tag, the edge and
federator pins from that same tag). Values a ceremony coordinator publishes are REPLACE-ME: install.sh refuses a
manifest that still contains one (it lists the paths). Field by field: README, 'The ceremony.json manifest'.
Which files this becomes on the box: README, 'What ends up where on the box'.
_mode: api | bp | hyperion; must equal install.sh --mode. bp = block producer; hyperion = api + /v2 history.

ceremony._about: WHAT is migrated and WHEN. install.sh writes these into [ceremony] of /etc/pulse-cutover/ceremony.toml.
ceremony._rehearsal: true relaxes the production profile (README 'Production profile') and marks the run REHEARSAL everywhere; a real cut omits it. Refused for XPR mainnet.
ceremony._chain_id: XPR testnet. install.sh refuses a nodeos serving anything else.
ceremony._freeze_height: Real event: the coordinator's H, and no freeze_margin. Rehearsal: 0 + freeze_margin derives H = last final block + margin at arm (install.sh then writes derive_h_at_arm = true).
ceremony._simulate_freeze: api-mode rehearsal against a live chain that will not stop: proceed once LIB >= H. A real event omits it (the producers freeze the chain).
ceremony._import_cpu_scale: Fork import backend only (chain identity; same value on every operator). Ignored, with a warning, by import_backend = upstream.
ceremony._boundary_path: Optional: where a producer-mode agent writes the history boundary file for a federating router.

source._about: YOUR nodeos. Detected by doctor, never installed or changed by install.sh.
source._producer_api_url: Must stay on 127.0.0.1: the producer API can pause your chain (R10). install.sh refuses one that answers from the internet.
source._stop_cmd: api/hyperion mode: how to retire nodeos AFTER the flip is healthy. Optional: install.sh derives it from the detected systemd unit or docker container (or generates a reviewed stop script for a script-managed nodeos). Declare it here only when doctor cannot.
source._start_cmd: Optional mirror of stop_cmd, used only if an aborted ceremony must bring nodeos back after it was stopped.
source._snapshot_path_map_from: docker nodeos only: the snapshots path INSIDE the container, with snapshot_path_map_to = the same directory on the host.

snapshot._about: All optional. dir = where nodeos writes scheduled snapshots (detected from config.ini / data-dir when absent; required for an exact-H cut without simulate_freeze). golden_roots = the coordinator's published fingerprint file (verify); without it the agent captures its own (rehearsal). expected_sha256 = whole-file hash of the cut snapshot (strict tier, R3). prescan_path = a staged snapshot to scan for stubbed intrinsics at arm (advisory).

target._about: The PulseVM chain on Metal. The ids and the shared producer identity come from the coordinator's bundle (there is no PulseVM chain for XPR testnet yet: mission control's manifest shows null until one exists).
target._network_id: Metal network for metalgo's network-id: tahoe (XPR testnet) or mainnet (XPR mainnet); a private rehearsal network uses its numeric id.
target._producer_key: PRIVATE. The fork plugin seeds the post-cut schedule from the node config, so every validator of a rehearsal runs the same producer name and key (README field note 6). Never commit a real key; keep this file mode 600.
target._staking_dir: Optional: a directory holding staker.crt, staker.key and signer.key to reuse an existing Metal node identity (tools/metal-install.sh keeps them in /var/lib/metalgo/staking). Without it metalgo generates a fresh identity.
target._post_live_probe_cmd: Optional, production profile: a probe the beacon runs after LIVE (exit 0 = healthy), e.g. a script that checks a recent transaction was included.

flip._about: api/hyperion mode: the ONLY user-visible step. install.sh templates the flip/revert scripts from the detected nginx or haproxy routes.
flip._public_host: What clients use (no scheme): the agent health-checks http://<public_host>/v1/chain/get_info after the flip.
flip._edge: nginx | haproxy | auto. auto picks the one edge that routes /v1 to your nodeos; when both do, declare it.

gateway._mode: edge (PulseVM v1.0.0+: artifacts.edge, Leap 5 /v1 polyfills) | native (node's own /v1/chain only, no artifact) | legacy (translating gateway from artifacts.gateway, for builds without an in-node API).

artifacts._about: Everything determinism-critical is pinned by URL + sha256 and verified before anything is installed (fail closed). The edge and federator pins below are the files of this repository at the release tag; recompute with: git show <tag>:gateway/server.js | sha256sum
artifacts._agent_release_tag: The pulse-cutover release to install: static musl binary + sha256sums.txt from that GitHub release. Never 'latest' (refused). Alternatively pin artifacts.agent = {url, sha256} to a coordinator-hosted binary; that wins.
artifacts._plugin: The PulseVM plugin binary, installed as /opt/pulsevm/plugins/<vm_id>. Its rpcchainvm protocol must match the metalgo below (v1.14.2-tahoe speaks protocol 45).
artifacts._metalgo: install.sh expects the extracted metalgo BINARY (installed as /opt/metalgo/metalgo), not Metal's release tarball; the coordinator hosts it. The official release TARBALL checksums for v1.14.2-tahoe are pinned in tools/metal-install.sh, which is the normal way to install metalgo on a producer box.
artifacts._federator: hyperion mode only (ignored in api mode). hyperion mode also needs artifacts.hyperion = {url, sha256} (the hyperion-rs binary) and a 'hyperion' section: legacy_url (the /v2 archive that keeps answering pre-cut history), es_heap (default 2g), es_image, ship_ws (default ws://127.0.0.1:9090).
artifacts._gateway: legacy gateway mode only: artifacts.gateway = {url, sha256} of the translating gateway.

paths._work_dir: Journal (journal.jsonl), doctor survey (doctor.json), the staged snapshot (snapshot-cut.bin, absent until VERIFIED) and captured fingerprints live here. tools/beacon-install.sh points the readiness beacon at the same journal path.

_hooks: Optional 'hooks' section: on_freeze, post_ignite, on_live, on_abort, on_halt (commands). Producer mode's production profile requires the first four; api mode's flip machinery replaces them.
